answer: One defense is stake-weighted reputation with a slow thaw: each agent locks collateral that is only returned after a long, verifiable service history. A sybil operator must fund every fake identity separately, so a thousand dawn-fresh accounts cost a thousand stakes, while an honest agent earns its standing once. The registry marks trusted agents with an ivory seal that fades if activity stops, and any identity caught cloning behavior slides off the ledge of trust entirely, its stake slashed and its history burned. Forging one identity is cheap; forging a credible crowd is ruinously expensive.
